rich_summary: Bhishma narrates the final ascent of Suka, the son of Vyasa, as he completes his yogic quest for liberation. Having realized the path of Emancipation, Suka enters profound meditation, transcends space, and travels through the sky with the brilliance of fire and the swiftness of thought. Celestial beings—Rishis, Apsaras, Gandharvas, and gods—watch in awe as nature itself honors him with flowers and reverence. Detached from all worldly ties, he asks the universe to answer his father if Vyasa calls after him. Casting off successively the qualities of tamas, rajas, and even sattva, Suka reaches the attributeless state of Brahman. Cosmic disturbances mark the moment of his transcendence, and with unstoppable force he even splits the joined peaks of Meru and Himavat, symbolizing the soul’s passage beyond all barriers into ultimate liberation.

top_scenes.scene_text: Suka, radiant like the sun, flying across the sky while gods, Rishis, and Apsaras watch in awe and celestial flowers rain down from heaven.
The ascetic Suka smashing through the joined golden and silver peaks of Meru and Himavat as the heavens erupt with cries of 'Excellent!'
Cosmic upheaval at the moment of Suka’s transcendence—earth trembling, meteors streaking, fragrant winds blowing as he dissolves into the attributeless Brahman.
